rv.q: This production is a blaze of colour at a dismally grey time.
It’s an enjoyable night out, and a brilliantly unlikely story, but in terms of the craft of musical theatre, Kinky Boots leans towards the pedestrian.
I feel like a heel for saying it but this Kinky Boots is soulless.
Radebe and Cardle knock this Kinky Boots out of the park.
Joyous and uplifting, Kinky Boots is just the tonic in an increasingly divided and divisive world.
Everyone gives their absolute all to ensure the audience have a jolly good time.
A gloriously fun night in the theatre which I would love to see again.
But neither book nor songs offer enough to buy a ticket to a show that leans lazily into the North in Northampton - complete with flat caps, vests and tats, and wayward accents.

cn.t: Radebe's magnetic performance as Lola elevates this uneven revival, though critics remain divided on the show's formulaic story and Lauper's score. Foster's production brings energy, but some find the material itself remains mediocre.
